summary: SSE stream truncated after mobile network switch; final tokens lost on reconnect
description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reports that long-running SSE streams (chat completions) are consistently losing the final choice when the mobile client switches network (cell <-> wifi) and reconnects. The client reconnect flow uses the resume token and expects the final '\n' framed 'end' event.

Impact: Multiple customers using BrightDocs' mobile app see truncated final sentences or missing final choice metadata, leading to confusing user-facing outputs. Affects production traffic in us-east-1.

Environment: prod API endpoint behind ALB and Fastly CDN; streaming endpoint path /v1/streams, gzip allowed at CDN edge; clients are Android app versions 5.3.1 and 5.3.2.

Observed behavior: On network handover, client reconnects with previous resume token but server sends a chunk that appears to merge the terminal event into an earlier chunk boundary. Client receives duplicated partial tokens then an immediate EOF from the CDN edge; final choice is not reconstructed.

Expected behavior: Resume should re-send missing tokens and terminate with a clear 'end' event/EOF; no partial duplication or dropped terminal events.

Temporary workaround: BrightDocs disabled aggressive client retry and implemented a 500ms backoff before resume to reduce overlapping connections; also disabled CDN gzip for streaming paths as a stopgap.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long streaming chat completion (>6s output) against /v1/streams using SSE from Android 5.3.1 on mobile network.
2) While stream is mid-output, toggle device from mobile data to wifi (or simulate poor network causing transient TCP close).
3) Client reconnects immediately with last resume token; observe SSE frames received at client and any duplicated partials or missing 'end' event.
4) Capture edge logs from Fastly and ALB, and a tcpdump of the server-facing connection for correlation.
logs: [server] resume validation: token=tok_ghjkl offset=10240 accepted=true session=brdoc-432
[server] stream_end emitted but last_event_boundary=offset(10176) < resume_offset(10240) => possible split
comments: 2026-03-12 14:35 - Aisha Gupta (Support): Customer reports reproducible on Android 5.3.1; attached tcpdump and Fastly edge logs. They see duplicated partial tokens and missing final choice metadata. Asked SRE to triage.

2026-03-12 15:02 - Marco Reyes (SRE): Initial hypothesis: CDN gzip + ALB chunk coalescing is shifting SSE event boundaries so resume_offset points inside a gzipped chunk; on reconnect Fastly serves an EOF and client can't reassemble. Requesting raw (ungzipped) edge-body for sample request. Assigned to me to investigate further.

2026-03-12 16:10 - Elena Park (BrightDocs): Replicated in our staging where Fastly configured identically; disabling gzip at edge fixed the missing-final-choice behavior consistently. We can keep gzip off if you recommend changes on your side.

2026-03-13 09:20 - Marco Reyes (SRE): Deployed temporary rule to strip gzip on /v1/streams for affected customer in us-east-1. Monitoring for 24h; raising follow-up to runtime team for robust resume-offset validation + chunk-normalization.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: resume offset validation assumes raw chunk boundaries from origin; CDN/ALB rewrites (gzip compression and chunk aggregation) can move event boundaries so offset points inside a compressed block -> client receives truncated token set.

Evidence: Fastly edge logs show gzipped=yes and early edge-close immediately after last server chunk. tcpdump from origin shows server emitted correct 'end' event but ALB/Fastly coalesced it into prior packet; gzipping at edge changed byte offsets.

Repro: Reproduced locally by introducing gzip at reverse proxy and toggling connection; client resume-side code fails to find 'end' marker when resume_offset > actual boundary due to recompression, producing partial duplicate deltas.
Mitigation tested: disabling gzip at CDN for streaming paths yields correct resume behavior; adding conservative client-side backoff reduces overlap-caused races but doesn't fix boundary mismatch.
Root cause candidate: mismatch between origin's resume offset semantics and CDN/proxy transformations (gzip, chunk coalescing, keepalive close timing).
resolution: Mitigation applied: Disabled gzip at Fastly for /v1/streams in us-east-1 for BrightDocs; customer confirmed immediate improvement in sample tests.

Short-term action: Add resume-offset validation in API gateway (detect if requested offset falls inside a transformed chunk) and return 409 with suggestion to re-fetch from safe offset if mismatch detected.

Long-term action: Runtime/Serving team to implement chunk-normalization: ensure server emits canonical, gzip-safe chunk boundaries or include explicit resume markers separate from byte offsets. Also add integration test that runs through CDN gzip path.
Next steps: Create INT ticket for runtime work (INT-9012) and add e2e test in CI that simulates CDN gzip/ALB behavior. Notify platform/console teams to show resume-failure metrics in Redwood Console.
